html:
The quartz crisis was the collapse of the Swiss watch industry in the 1970s, when cheap battery-powered quartz watches from Japan and the United States took the market.

Watchmaking came to Geneva with Huguenot refugees in the 1500s and spread through the Jura valleys. By the 1960s Switzerland made about half the world's watches. The first quartz wristwatch, the Seiko Astron, went on sale in Japan in 1969. The Swiss had built a quartz prototype themselves but had not pushed it. Jobs in the industry fell by about two thirds.

Rescue came in 1983 with the cheap plastic Swatch and a merger of the big makers led by Nicolas Hayek. The industry survived by selling mechanical watches as luxury goods, and Switzerland now leads the world by value. Compare the earlier rise of Swiss made precision.
sum: The quartz crisis was the collapse of the Swiss watch industry in the 1970s, when cheap battery-powered quartz watches from Japan and the United States took the market.
